concepts.def: Vectors have direction (force, velocity); scalars don't (mass, speed).
The turning effect of a force: moment = force × perpendicular distance.
Independent horizontal and vertical motion under gravity.
Impulse = change in momentum = force × time.
Stress ÷ strain, a measure of stiffness.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Further Mechanics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Further Mechanics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Further Mechanics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A car travels 4 km north then 3 km east. What is its displacement magnitude?
options: 7 km
5 km
1 km
25 km

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Acceleration
Momentum
Kinetic energy
Weight

mcqs.q: In what direction does a magnetic field exert a force on a current-carrying wire?
options: The force is in the same direction as the magnetic field.
The force is in the same direction as the current in the wire.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
Perpendicular to both the current direction and the magnetic field direction (Fleming's left hand rule).

mcqs.q: If the distance between two masses doubles, what happens to the gravitational force between them?
options: It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
It halves — gravitational force is inversely proportional to distance.
It quarters — gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency not eject electrons?
options: Enough low-frequency photons should eventually eject an electron if you wait long enough.
Each photon's energy is below the work function; many low-energy photons can't combine to eject an electron.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
The force is in the same direction as the current in the wire.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Displacement”?
options: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Vector”?
options: The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Acceleration”?
options: Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Velocity”?
options: Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resolving vectors”?
options: Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Scalar”?
options: Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
